text:
Maria G.: Heads-up — the per-model burn dashboard just spiked for prod routes  /chat and /summarize in eu-west-1 around 02:10 UTC.
Ajay R.: saw that too. dashboard shows +42% token spend vs baseline for last 4h. any deploys around then?
Kevin L.: no prod deploys in that window from infra. I saw a couple of scale-up events for dedicated pools in eu-west though.
Priya S.: are we sure the dashboard is attributing by route correctly? last week we had a tag mapping issue where model->route mapping doubled cost for some requests.
Diego: tagging bug would make sense. I can run a quick query to compare request counts vs tokens billed per route.
Maria G.: please. the FinOps view shows tokens billed >> tokens served for /summarize (x1.8). that smells like double-counting or cross-region replication billing.
finops-bot: Daily FinOps snapshot uploaded: https://redwood.internal/finops/snapshots/2024-05-07 — per-route CSV attached. (uploaded by finops-bot)
Ajay R.: downloading.. quick check: are we routing fallback requests to reserved-capacity variants that are billed differently? e.g., routed to dedicated pool with different billing profile.
Kevin L.: possible — smart routing can fallback to dedicated GPUs in eu-west when hosted capacity low. If requests hit both hosted + dedicated within same logical trace, the attribution layer might mis-aggregate.
Priya S.: Diego — SQL to run: compare model_request_count and billing_token_sum grouped by route, region, model_variant. Something like:
```
SELECT route, region, model_variant, count(*) AS reqs, sum(tokens) AS tokens_served, sum(billed_tokens) AS tokens_billed
FROM request_logs
WHERE ts BETWEEN '2024-05-07T01:00:00Z' AND '2024-05-07T04:00:00Z'
GROUP BY 1,2,3
ORDER BY tokens_billed DESC
```
Diego: running now. will paste results in a sec.
Maria G.: also check reserved capacity commit tagging (commit_id) — I want to see if committed pool usage is being double-counted as on-demand in the billing export.
finops-bot: quick note: GCP/AWS billing exports sometimes show the same GPU usage under both "CommittedUsage" and "OnDemand" for cross-account shared pools. CC @finance-team.
Diego: pasted top 3 rows: `/chat` eu-west-1 model-x-dedicated reqs: 18k tokens_served: 2.1M tokens_billed: 3.8M; `/summarize` eu-west-1 model-x-hosted reqs: 12k tokens_served: 1.4M tokens_billed: 1.4M; `/chat` eu-west-1 model-x-hosted reqs: 9k tokens_served: 1.0M tokens_billed: 1.0M.
Ajay R.: so the dedicated variant is showing billed tokens >> served tokens (3.8M vs 2.1M). that looks like duplication on billing export for dedicated pools.
Kevin L.: can we map the commit_id on those dedicated nodes to the billing export lines? maybe commit id mismatched region label (eu-west vs eu-west-1a) causing aggregator to treat them as separate resources.
Priya S.: I'm suspicious of a tagging drift during the autoscaler expansion — tags might have been applied after instance spin-up, so first X minutes of usage weren't associated with the reserved pool and got billed as on-demand.
Maria G.: operational ask: Diego/Kevin — please create a short reconciled report (per-route, per-model, per-region) with columns: reqs, tokens_served, tokens_billed, billing_resource_id, commit_id. Put it in the FinOps channel when done.
Diego: will do. ETA 30m. I'll also grep the autoscaler logs for tag application timestamps.
Kevin L.: I'll open a billing case with cloud support if we find lines where the same instance shows both committed and on-demand usage. need to confirm before escalating.
Ajay R.: FYI we should also add a short alert in the dashboard: if tokens_billed/tokens_served > 1.2 for any route -> fire a FinOps ticket.
Priya S.: agree. can we implement a temporary dashboard marker and a daily reconciler job to flag anomalies? I can add the alert if you grant me edit perms.
Maria G.: granted. make the alert but set snooze for 1h so it's not noisy while we investigate.
finops-bot: noted. created ticket FINOPS-847 in the backlog and added the snapshot link.
Diego: uploaded reconciled CSV to the ticket. key finding: 98% of the discrepancy is from 3 dedicated node IDs with commit_id null in the billing export. looks like tag propagation issue.
Kevin L.: opened cloud billing support case with the three instance IDs. provided CSV and timestamps. support asked for billing export raw lines — uploaded.
Ajay R.: great work. action items: 1) infra to add tag-propagation check to autoscaler (Kevin/Diego) 2) dashboard alert (Priya) 3) finops to validate reserved vs on-demand mapping (Maria/Ajay). I'll track in FINOPS-847.
Maria G.: thanks everyone. looping in sales only if customer-facing SLA impacted. for now mark as internal cost investigation. :thumbsup:
Priya S.: will follow up when alert is live.
Diego: will update the ticket after cloud support responds.
Maria G.: closing thread for now, will reopen if billing support finds charge reversals.
